question: On Bank of America's second-quarter 2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026), what full-year 2026 outlook did the CFO give for (a) net interest income (NII) growth and (b) operating leverage, and how did each compare with the outlook he said had been given earlier in 2026 (in January and/or April)?
grading: Key points (all required): (1) full-year 2026 NII growth expected at the UPPER END of the 6%-8% range (not a new numeric range); (2) full-year 2026 operating leverage expected in the range of 300 to 400 basis points; (3) comparison with earlier outlook: NII growth was 5%-7% in January and raised to 6%-8% in April; operating leverage was 'more than 200 basis points' as of the April (Q1) call. Accept equivalent wording ('top end of 6-8%', '3-4 percentage points'). Fail if the answer gives plain 6%-8% or 5%-7% as the current NII view without 'upper end', gives 'more than 200 bps' as the current operating-leverage view, states a dollar NII figure as guidance, or relies on remarks from the Q3 2026 call (mid-October 2026, after the as_of date) or the mid-September Barclays conference.
answer: (a) Full-year 2026 NII growth is now expected at the upper end of the 6%-8% range (the CFO recalled 5%-7% in January, raised to 6%-8% in April) [W01-E1]. (b) Full-year 2026 operating leverage is now expected to be 300 to 400 basis points, up from 'more than 200 basis points' given on the April call; first-half 2026 operating leverage had already exceeded 450 bps (Q2: 6.6%) [W01-E1]. Neither full-year outlook appears in the July 14 press release or in the slide deck filed with the 8-K [W01-E2, W01-E3].

output.answer:
**Bank of America Q2 2026 earnings call — July 14, 2026 (CFO Alastair Borthwick)**

**(a) Full-year 2026 net interest income (NII) growth**
- **New outlook:** NII growth for full-year 2026 is expected **at the upper end of the 6%–8% range** (vs. 2025). Drivers cited: anticipated loan and deposit growth, fixed-rate asset repricing, and balance sheet optimization. The guidance assumes modest loan/deposit growth in H2 and the then-current forward curve (one 25 bp hike in September).
- **Prior outlooks:** In **January**, BAC guided to **5%–7%** full-year NII growth. In **April**, it **raised the range to 6%–8%**. So the July update is an upgrade within/above the April range (top end) and a clear step up from January's 5%–7%.

**(b) Full-year 2026 operating leverage**
- **New outlook:** **300–400 basis points**, after first-half 2026 operating leverage exceeded **450 bps**.
- **Prior outlook:** On the **Q1 (April) call**, Borthwick guided to **more than 200 bps** for the full year. He also noted that at Investor Day the bank had committed to **200–300 bps** of operating leverage over the next three-to-five years. So the July figure is an increase from ">200 bps" (and above the longer-term 200–300 bps commitment).

**Summary of comparisons**
| Metric | January 2026 guide | April 2026 guide | July 14, 2026 guide |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY26 NII growth | 5%–7% | 6%–8% (raised) | Upper end of 6%–8% (raised again) |
| FY26 operating leverage | ~>200 bps (consistent with prior) | >200 bps (reiterated) | 300–400 bps (raised) |

We now expect... upper end"; "On our first quarter earnings call in April, we told you we expected full-year operating leverage of more than 200 basis points... we now expect full-year operating leverage to be in the range of 300-400 basis points"): https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/bac/transcripts/649666-q2-2026 ; https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BAC/earnings/BAC-Q2-2026-earnings_call-649666.html
- Reuters (July 14, 2026): https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/bank-america-profit-rises-trading-boost-2026-07-14
- Q1 2026 call highlights (April guidance: NII raised to 6%–8%; >200 bps operating leverage): https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/04/17/bank-of-america-q1-earnings-call-highlights.html ; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bank-america-q1-earnings-call-190422400.html
